answer: One workable check ties each agent to a single stake-backed vertex in a shared reputation graph, so a new copy starts with no history and cannot borrow trust from its siblings. The vertex only gains weight after real completed jobs, and its score decays when the agent goes quiet, which keeps old farming runs from sitting at their zenith forever. Honest agents can earn their way into a haven of trusted work, but a fresh sybil cluster has to pay the same slow cost again for every copy, and that cost is what makes mass duplication unprofitable.
